Apple Unveils First MacBook Pro with a Touchscreen and OLED Display

On October 28, 2026, at its "Pro and Tell" event in Los Angeles, Apple announced new MacBook Pro models featuring a PROLED XDR display. These are the first Mac laptops to support touch input and utilize a tandem OLED screen. The 14-inch model starts at $2,899 (with the M5 Pro chip), while the 16-inch model begins at $3,399 (also with the M5 Pro). Configurations featuring the M5 Max chip start at $4,499 and $4,799, respectively. Pre-orders open on October 28, with shipments beginning November 6.

The display offers brightness of up to 2,000 nits (for both HDR and SDR content), a contrast ratio of 10,000,000:1, and an adaptive refresh rate ranging from 10 Hz to 120 Hz (ProMotion). The touch sensor is integrated directly into the display panel. New features include the "Dynamic Island," an illuminated Apple logo on the lid, and a lighter chassis (the 14-inch model weighs approximately 1.36 kg). The devices are powered by the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips found in previous models, supporting up to 128 GB of RAM and up to 16 TB of storage. They are available in Space Black and Silver, with an optional nano-texture glass finish.

In the days leading up to the event, Apple also introduced an updated iPad mini (8th generation), featuring an 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, a thinner 5.4 mm chassis, IP67-rated protection, and a new speaker system. The starting price is $699 (for the Wi-Fi model with 128 GB of storage). In addition, a 14-inch MacBook Pro and an iMac powered by the M6 ​​chip were announced (with starting prices of $1,999 and $1,499, respectively). These devices will go on sale during the same timeframe.

📌 Atomic Swaps: Exchanging Crypto Without Trusting an Intermediary

Main Points
⏺ Atomic swaps allow participants to exchange assets without handing funds to a centralized custodian
⏺ The mechanism is designed so both sides receive their assets or the exchange doesn't complete
⏺ This post explains why atomic swaps are an interesting approach to decentralized trading

1️⃣ Core Idea — two users want to exchange assets from different blockchains without trusting an exchange or intermediary with their funds.
2️⃣ How It Works — one approach uses cryptographic secrets and time restrictions to coordinate an exchange under predefined rules.
3️⃣ Main Advantage — participants don't need to transfer custody of their assets to a third party during the exchange.
4️⃣ The Challenges — networks need compatible mechanisms, while participants need liquidity, time, and correct execution.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — before swapping, review fees on both chains, lock periods, technical requirements, and refund conditions.

Final Thoughts

Atomic swaps aim to solve a fundamental crypto problem: how to exchange value with a stranger without relying on their honesty.

🔔 Bitcoin price reclaims $80K as US GDP beats forecasts 

📣 Bitcoin price has reclaimed the $80,000 level after briefly falling below it earlier on Thursday, as fresh US economic data showed stronger than expected growth in the third quarter and persistent inflation in September. The latest figures arrived a day after the Federal Reserve decided to leave interest rates unchanged, raising fresh questions about whether the central bank could consider another rate hike before the end of the year.

⚠️ Bitcoin (BTC) had dropped to approximately $79,800 earlier in the session before recovering above $80,000. However, the cryptocurrency remained under pressure following Wednesday’s Fed decision, with traders assessing how the latest economic figures could affect monetary policy. Thursday’s advance GDP estimate showed that the US economy grew faster in the third quarter, supported mainly by consumer spending, business investment, and government expenditure.

🌐 Business investment remained another contributor, particularly as technology companies continued spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure and equipment. However, the stronger economic performance was accompanied by inflation figures that showed consumer prices continued to rise in September. The Fed’s preferred inflation measure, the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, rose 0.5% month over month, compared with a 0.3% increase in August.

👀 Tether has led a $15 million Series A funding round for New York-based Mural, supporting the financial technology company’s development of payment infrastructure for businesses and artificial intelligence agents. Mural plans to use the investment to expand internationally and develop the banking, payment and compliance services needed for software agents to conduct financial transactions.

🔔 Founded in 2022 by former Palantir engineers Sinclair Toffa and Chris Fernandes, the company provides infrastructure that businesses use to manage accounts, payment instructions, identity verification and regulatory requirements across banking networks and blockchains. Its customers include global payroll provider Deel, browser developer Opera and financial technology platform Axexo. Through Mural’s system, businesses can offer accounts holding dollars, local currencies and stablecoins without managing separate financial infrastructure for each payment method.

📌 The company reported processing $2.1 billion in payments for users across 128 countries since introducing its application programming interface in 2025. Payment volume recorded so far in 2026 is nearly six times its total for 2025. Mural has not disclosed the valuation attached to the latest funding round. Fortune reported that the company previously raised $5 million in seed financing in 2022, followed by additional capital from existing backers.
